newsitem.title: JAPAN: New reactors spotlight ageing N.Korea power grid.
newsitem.headline: New reactors spotlight ageing N.Korea power grid.

text.p: The international community's $4.5 billion construction of two nuclear reactors in North Korea may require billions of dollars in further investment to revamp the cash-strapped country's ageing power grid, analysts say.

The project, undertaken by the multinational Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO), was conceived under an agreement between Pyongyang and Washington in 1994 aimed at halting North Korea's suspected development of nuclear weapons and fostering better economic ties between North and South Korea.

KEDO -- comprised initially of the United States, Japan, and South Korea but expanded to include Australia, Canada, Chile, Finland, Indonesia, New Zealand and the European Union -- held an official ground-breaking ceremony in North Korea on Tuesday.
Construction of the two 1,000 megawatt light-water reactors began on August 19 and is expected to take seven to 10 years.

But nuclear industry analysts say North Korea's non-computerised and rusting network of power lines will not be able to sustain all of the electricity generated by the two reactors without a fiscal shot in the arm that could amount to billions of dollars.
